summary: Feed s076_single is degraded for IDS: 21.9% of TCP sessions are one-way (33/151), exceeding 10% threshold. IDS requires bidirectional traffic for stateful inspection. All other checks (duplicates, encryption, VLAN, drops, overload, truncation, tunnels, oversize) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/SPAN is forwarding only one direction of TCP sessions to the IDS tool port. Most likely cause is incomplete aggregation - client-to-server and server-to-client directions are split across different tool ports, or capture is from a single-direction SPAN/TAP, or asymmetric routing with single-sided capture. 33 of 151 sessions affected.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP reassembly, stream tracking, and signature matching. With 21.9% one-way flows, IDS cannot correlate request/response, misses attacks that span both directions, loses detection coverage and generates incomplete session logs.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS tool port using 5-tuple hashing on the packet broker so the IDS sees complete bidirectional sessions for stateful analysis.
